questions.question: When downshifting, what should you do?

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way to neutral first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, shift down one gear at a time. Ease out the clutch slowly between each shift.

questions.question: The body gets rid of about one drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are probably still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals about four drinks remaining.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: Can common drugs like cold tablets affect a rider's ability to ride safely?

options.text: Yes, they can affect a rider's ability to ride safely.
No, because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect a rider's ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Most drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Know the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: What kind of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Can low-speed crashes be serious?

options.text: No, they happen so often that they are not a concern.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can cause death.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Clothes that cover your arms and legs completely.
Clothes that cover your arms completely but leave your legs exposed.
Clothes that cover your legs completely but leave your arms exposed.
Whatever is most comfortable, even if it is not safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothes that cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs to protect yourself.

questions.question: Which organization's certification should a helmet have for maximum protection?
questions.explanation: Choose a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for the best protection.

questions.question: What is it called when you shift to a lower gear?
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows the motorcycle like braking does. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Which surface provides good traction for tires?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all provide poor traction. Dry pavement provides the best grip for tires.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride normally, since all bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Learn how the gears work on this specific motorcycle.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be used on curves.
Should use the road shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The extra wheel changes how the bike handles curves.

questions.question: Checking your mirrors:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be done regularly as part of your normal riding routine.
Does not help because you cannot control what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done regularly as part of your normal riding routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while riding. Always check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: During daytime riding, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only when it is cloudy.
Use your headlight only if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Always use your headlight, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead:

options.text: When it is harder to stop than normal.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to pass you.
So the driver ahead does not know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is harder to stop than normal.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space when stopping will be difficult. This includes wet pavement, when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and other drivers may cut in front of you.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Both brakes at the same time.
Either brake, but never both together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when stopping. Using both brakes at once gives you the best stopping power.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: Drag your feet on the ground.
Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
Keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: For good balance, keep your feet firmly on the footrests. Do not drag your feet or point your toes down, as this may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly.

questions.question: Long-term wind noise from riding:

options.text: Is safer than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have which types of brakes?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel—a front brake and a rear brake. The front brake provides more stopping power.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should be done:
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This takes only a few minutes and helps prevent safety problems before you ride.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing so other drivers can see you. Bright colors work during the day and at night.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black letters show traffic rules like speed limits. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Riding alongside a car:

options.text: Can place you in a blind spot.
Is not an issue unless the road is wet.
Can make driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can place you in a blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the car will block your escape route.

questions.question: If you wait an hour per alcoholic drink before you ride your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system. This buildup can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass when you can. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate faster, which increases the danger.
